counterevidence_considered.description: The only candidate for hidden shared structure is that the twelve single-night surveys span roughly 20 days of one breeding season, so seasonal drift in sunset time or phenology could induce temporal correlation among rows; however, every survey_date is unique to exactly one pond, so this is at most an unmodelled covariate concern and not a repeated entry of any independent unit into the row-independent procedure.

evidence.description: The input table contains exactly 12 data rows with 12 distinct pond_id values (BRW-01 through BRW-12); no pond identifier appears on more than one line, so no independent unit contributes more than one row to the analysis.

The workflow explicitly guards against repeated entry of the same independent unit: it tracks seen pond_id values and raises a ValueError if any pond appears more than once, and it appends exactly one onset value per row, so the row-independent Mann-Whitney procedure receives one observation per pond.
evidence.observed_value: read_onsets() raises on duplicate pond_id and appends one value per row

seen = set()
    with INPUT_PATH.open(newline="", encoding="ascii") as handle:
        for row in csv.DictReader(handle):
            pond = row["pond_id"]
            if pond in seen:
                raise ValueError("pond appears more than once: " + pond)
            seen.add(pond)
            onsets[row[GROUP_COLUMN]].append(float(row[ONSET_COLUMN]))

evidence.description: The data description states that pond_id is the independent-unit column, that each code occurs on exactly one line, that no pond was revisited or split across lines, and that a procedure treating lines as independent observations suits this table; the grouping variable varies between ponds only.
evidence.observed_value: one row per pond by design; row-independent procedure declared suitable

source_refs.quoted_text:
Twelve ponds contribute twelve lines, one apiece. No pond was revisited, no
pond is split across lines, and no two ponds were surveyed on the same date,
so every onset value comes from a different source. Ponds are separate water
bodies in separate catchments and were not paired or matched with each other.
A procedure that treats the lines as independent observations therefore suits
this table, and the grouping variable (lighting regime) varies between ponds
rather than within any pond.

evidence.description: The reported selected result is exactly reproducible from one observation per pond: lit onsets {35,44,51,58,63,70} versus unlit {12,19,23,27,31,38} give U = 35, exact two-sided p = 4/924 = 0.00433, rank-biserial = 2*35/36 - 1 = 0.944, medians 54.5 versus 25.0, and group sizes n = 6 and 6, matching the report; no inflation of effective sample size beyond the 12 authorized units is present.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Mann-Whitney U test of chorus onset, lit (n = 6) versus unlit (n = 6) ponds: U = 35.0, exact two-sided p = 0.00433, rank-biserial correlation = 0.944; onset is later at lit ponds (median 54.5 versus 25.0 minutes after sunset).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue class by searching for any route through which one pond could enter the Mann-Whitney procedure more than once: (1) scanned all 12 data rows of data/input.csv for duplicate pond_id values or a pond split across lines — all 12 identifiers are distinct and each date is unique; (2) traced workflow/analysis.py end to end — read_onsets() appends exactly one float per CSV row, raises ValueError on any repeated pond_id, and no loop, resampling, merge, or concatenation reuses a value, so each group list holds one entry per pond; (3) recomputed the test from raw values assuming one observation per pond and reproduced the reported U = 35.0, exact two-sided p = 0.00433, rank-biserial = 0.944, group sizes 6 and 6, and both medians and means exactly, which would not match if any unit had been entered repeatedly. All attempts to establish repeated authorized-unit entry failed.
